clips.text: Your tongue has around ten thousand taste buds — and it can also see.
He is blind. He has never seen a rock wall. But he is climbing one — and he is reading every hold with his tongue.
Four hundred tiny pulses on his tongue — and within fifteen minutes, he can tell where things are. A doorway. A cup. A face.
He plays tic-tac-toe with his daughter. He reads letters off cards. He climbs — seeing the wall through his tongue.
The camera films the world. His tongue feels the picture. And fifteen minutes later, the wall makes sense.
So why can your tongue work as a second pair of eyes?
Your brain builds the picture, not your eyes — and the price is you can't taste while you see.
